title: Rose motif — layered
subtitle: Three separate petal layers sewn together at the centre, 8 cm
excerpt: Three rounds of petals — small, medium, and large — are worked separately and stacked at the centre with a tapestry needle, then anchored through a dc ring base. The layered construction gives a more open, open-bloom look than the rolled rose, and the three petal sizes make the flower believably natural in scale.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 6 (1891), built-up flower motif chapter (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crocheted flower construction.

chartDefinition.title: Rose motif — layered
chartDefinition.caption: Three separate petal rings worked individually: inner ring (5-petal, htr), middle ring (5-petal, tr), outer ring (5-petal, dtr). Each ring has its own magic ring. Rings are stacked and anchored at the centre.

glossaryTerms.definition: A taller stitch than a treble, made with two yarn-overs before inserting the hook. UK double treble equals US treble. Used in the outer petal ring to give the largest petals height.

content.text: The layered rose builds three separate petal rings at different heights — half treble (inner), treble (middle), and
double treble

(outer) — and stacks them with the inner ring on top. Because each ring is worked separately, the petal count and colour on each layer can vary; the standard version uses five petals per ring in three tones of the same colour.

Work each ring individually, pull the magic ring tail closed, and weave in the end before stacking. Stack them outer-ring-down, middle on top, inner on top of that, then sew through all three centres with a tapestry needle to hold the arrangement. A button or bead in the very centre covers the sewing point.

attrs.title: Materials for one rose
attrs.body: About 3 g each of three tones of DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm crochet hook. Tapestry needle. Scissors. One small button or bead for the centre (optional).

content.text: Gauge
Each finished layered rose measures 8 cm across in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.
Stitches used
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), magic ring (MR) — UK and US shared.
half treble (htr) — UK; US "half double crochet".
treble (tr) — UK; US "double crochet".
double treble (dtr) — UK; US "treble".
Pattern
Inner ring — darkest colour
Form a magic ring. *Ch 2. Work 4htr into the ring. Ch 2. Sl st into the ring.* Repeat from * to * four more times. (5 petals.) Pull tail to close. Fasten off.
Middle ring — mid-tone colour
Form a magic ring. *Ch 3. Work 5tr into the ring. Ch 3. Sl st into the ring.* Repeat from * to * four more times. (5 petals.) Pull tail to close. Fasten off.
Outer ring — lightest colour
Form a magic ring. *Ch 4. Work 6dtr into the ring. Ch 4. Sl st into the ring.* Repeat from * to * four more times. (5 petals.) Pull tail to close. Fasten off.
Assembly

Lay the outer ring flat. Place the middle ring on top, rotating it so its petals sit between the outer petals. Place the inner ring on top of the middle ring. Thread a tapestry needle with a length of any colour and take 4 stitches through the centre of all three rings. Sew a button or bead to the very top to cover the stitching point. Fasten off all sewing ends through the back of the outer ring.

definition.title: Rose motif — layered
definition.caption: Three separate five-petal rings. Inner: htr petals. Middle: tr petals. Outer: dtr petals. Stack and sew at centre.

content.text: Care
Handwash gently in cool water with mild soap. Lay flat on a towel and ease the petal layers apart while damp. The three-dimensional structure will reshape itself as it dries.
What to try next
The freestanding rose (crochet-rose-freestanding) works in the round in a single piece without stacking. Six petal rings instead of three give a more open bloom.
